# 1.2.95 - one style guide, one glossary and a text lint for every text the module shows, with a pilot of rewritten texts the owner read and approved; nothing changes at the table

Stage E65 ships alone with this version. 1.2.95 is built on 1.2.94 (E50 and E51), which shipped first (31.10.2026) and is
included here; these notes do not repeat it. E65 is for whoever writes or reviews the module's texts: a style guide, a
glossary that gives each term the stage from which it holds, budgets for how long each kind of text may be, a text lint
that reads every text the module shows, and the tools beside it. **It changes no module behaviour**: tools, documents,
tests and the lint only. In a pilot the owner read 40 rewritten texts and 60 Polish naturalness pairs and approved them
(01.11.2026); the approved texts are not in the game yet - E66 and E71 apply them. Nothing in this version has been run at
a real table or in Foundry; what was measured was measured on the headless harness. 25 commits on top of 1.2.94, up to
52d91f38, the last before the release commit, plus 3 merges that bring the 1.2.94 line (52eacb9c, 11fb3c97, 4a51c934).
What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world: nothing at the table.**
   - **No language key changes:** `lang/en.json` and `lang/pl.json` have no diff from 1.2.94. Nor do the handbooks, the
     style sheets or the macros.
   - **No runtime script changes.** The only files under `scripts/` that change are the suite's: `tests-text.mjs` (new),
     `tests-kit.mjs` and `tests-tier0.mjs`. They are reached only when a GM runs the suite (`game.drpg.runTests()`, through
     `api.mjs`'s dynamic import of the suite), never when the module starts. Tier 0 gains three tests that write nothing to
     the world, R1058, R1059 and R1060; R1060 puts the Polish over `config.mjs`'s English for the length of the test and
     checks that it put back what it found.
   - **No setting, no GM store, no migration, no socket or bridge action.** `settings.mjs`, `gm-stores.mjs`, `migrate.mjs`
     and the bridge's files are not among the changed files; the stage touched no socket, bridge action, roll, GM store or
     world write.
   - `module.json` has no diff from 1.2.94 (it still reads 1.2.94; the release commit sets the version).
   - **The package.** The guide, the glossary, the budgets, `docs/dev/` (the pilot's file and the review of older texts)
     and `tools/` stay out of module.zip (`.gitattributes`). With the last `.gitattributes` change of the stage,
     `git archive` listed the same 209 entries as before it.
   - **The stage ledger** (`tools/stages.json`): rows E65, E66, E68, E69, E71, E73 and E74, then E83 and E91; the
     `planned` of every unshipped row after 1.2.94 renumbered one per row from E65's 1.2.95 (E26 stays 1.3.0). This is
     information only; the release numbers stay the owner's. E65's own row declares `touches: []`.
3. **The owner's answers.**
   - **30.10.** The wording of the rules O1-O18, X1-X21, M1-M10, N1-N8 and of the 60 naturalness pairs was lost ("Nie mam
     juz cztery kierunki niestety..."). The owner's default holds: the guide is rebuilt from what survives, every rebuilt
     rule says that it is rebuilt and from what, no rebuilt rule is presented as the original, and the 60 pairs are
     written fresh for the owner to read.
   - **31.10 (D191).** Hope and Despair are masculine and indeclinable in Polish, as the texts already use them; the
     neuter that DB28 gives the resources does not cover them.
   - **01.11, the first pilot page (E65-PILOT-R1).** All 40 rewritten texts approved, with no note; the 8 questions on
     their defaults ("w pokoju {room}" for a room in Polish, "kafel" not a form for the room and voice tiles, "majstrowanie"
     the ordinary word, "Projekty" forbidden as a name, "Odrzuć" as built, no budget for settings names, MISIUBOMBO a
     report finding, T18's verb lists as built). A ninth question, the Frisk row's Polish form: "Propozycja c13 lepsza"
     (below).
   - **01.11, the second page (E65-PILOT-R2).** All 60 naturalness pairs approved as written: "Wszystkie z 60
     naturalnosci zatwierdzam jako domyslne".
   - **01.11, Q-E65-1.** "Tak dopiszmy": the lines the release commit adds to the repository's agent rules (below).
   - Q-E65-2 (the ledger's numbers) and Q-E65-4 (E65 ships only after the pilot; E66 and every stage that writes text wait
     for E65 to ship) on their defaults.

## For whoever writes or reviews the module's texts

- **The style guide, `docs/text-style.md`.** One source of style for every text the module shows - tiles, windows, cards,
  notifications, settings, diagnostics and handbooks, in English and in Polish - in 13 sections, in English, with section
  7 and section 12 in Polish. Every rule ends with exactly one status: *survives* (with its source quoted or named; the
  owner's DB answers are cited by number and bind as decided), *rebuilt 30.10 from* a named source, or *rebuilt 30.10 from the
  number alone*. When the guide was written (E65 C5) it held 110 rules: 49 survive, 30 were rebuilt from a named source
  and 31 from the number alone. The pilot confirmed 21 rules and 7 of section 3's 14 surface rows; the 60 pairs confirmed
  X1, X10, X13 and M8. A rule the pilot did not confirm reads "to confirm in E71 (row 1.2.128)": 37 rules, section 3's
  other seven rows and section 12's method. No rule reads "changed in the pilot": no verdict was a correction. Section 12
  holds the 60 naturalness pairs N1-N60 and "Wzorzec pozytywny", the 40 approved pairs as the positive model; section 13
  says why so much is rebuilt and lists what stays open, each item with the stage that owns it.
- **The glossary, `docs/glossary.json`.** 109 entries and 15 retired names. Each entry has its English and Polish form,
  gender, inflection, the forbidden variants with their scope, the stage from which it holds and its source; a missing or
  unknown stage, a missing field or a doubled id turns the lint red. Entries hold only once their stage has shipped, so a
  forbidden variant of an entry whose stage has not shipped is reported as not yet due, apart from the debt. Five entries are
  open (no source decides them; they forbid nothing): `db3-english`, `mechanic-capitals`, `truth-bullet`, `murder-weapon`
  and `gm-bar-buttons`.
  - **Hope and Despair** are masculine and indeclinable (D191), in the guide's Polish part and in their glossary entries.
  - **The Frisk row's Polish form is decided for E71:** "Zobacz, co ktoś nosi" ("zobacz, co ktoś nosi" in a sentence), the
    form a reviewer proposed and the owner took. The game still reads "Zobacz, co nosi"; E71 changes the five places with
    the old form (two values of `lang/pl.json`, three lines of the Polish handbooks) and the tier-1 test R620 that pins it.
    Until then the lint reports the five as not yet due.
- **The text budgets, `docs/text-budgets.json`.** 13 surfaces, each with a target and a limit of about 1.5 times the
  target (DB11); GM diagnostics have no limit and are reported only. Rules give a key its surface by its name or by the
  function that sends it; an allowed exception names its key, the rule, why, and the stage that may remove it. The
  numbers are rebuilt and read "to confirm in E71".
- **The text lint, `node tools/check.mjs text`.** A new part of `node tools/check.mjs`, and so of `npm run quick` and
  `npm test`. Each of its 26 detectors (`scripts/tests-text.mjs`) runs first on its own fixture, then over what it reads of
  the language files, `config.mjs`'s English prose, the scripts and every `.md` under `docs/`, one line each.
  - **FAIL now (red on a finding):** T1 (Polish four forms for each English plural family; a Config value's placeholders),
    T2 (the same placeholders and HTML tags in English and Polish), T3 (a plural family formatted or localized directly;
    a baseline of 1 row, emptied by E66), T6 (an en dash, an em dash or a minus sign in a text the module shows, also
    written as an HTML entity; a baseline of 11 rows, emptied by E25) and T14 (the item tables' words and legacy names).
  - **Report (printed, never red):** the other twenty, each with the stage that turns it to FAIL - E25 for T7's part and
    T8; E66 for T20 and T28; E71 for T4, T5, T11, T12, T13, T15, T16, T21, T24 and T25. T17, T18, T19, T22, T23 and T27
    stay report.
  - **Also red:** a detector that does not flag exactly its fixture, a detector that read nothing, a fault of a file E65
    writes (the glossary, the budgets, the guide's pairs table, the screen and audience maps, the pilot's file), and a
    handbook the facts tool cannot split. Where the pilot's 40 texts stand in the language files (still the before, the
    approved text applied, or changed since the pilot) is a reading, not red.
  - `--lang <dir>` reads `en.json` and `pl.json` from another folder; `--all` prints every report finding. It writes no
    file. Measured 01.11.2026 on 4 cores: 16 s alone, report found 3414.
- **The text tools** (`tools/`, in Node, writing under `audit/harness/results/text/`, which git ignores, unless `--out`
  names another file):
  - `node tools/text-map.mjs` - the screen map, which keys each window, card and flow shows: 146 scripts, 7044 units, 1059
    entry points, 126 screens; 5094 of 5289 keys assigned, 195 not.
  - `node tools/text-render.mjs` - every string filled the way a table fills it, in English and Polish (a Markdown file
    each and a Polish HTML sheet): 4785 keys in each language, 18652 strings, fixtures for 241 placeholder names, 0 unknown.
    `--pilot <file>` renders the owner's pilot sheet.
  - `node tools/text-audience.mjs` - who reads each key the module posts: 974 sends, 769 with a key, 93 wrappers; 1219 of
    5289 keys assigned.
  - `node tools/handbook-facts.mjs` - a handbook cut into units (paragraphs, table rows, notes) with stable ids, and
    `check`, `count`, `prompt` and `self` beside it, for E57's handbook facts. The English player handbook: 404 units in 17
    sections. Two fresh agents given the prompt on the player handbook's section 8 wrote 85 and 81 facts; after one
    tightening of the prompt, two more wrote 89 and 89.
- **Three tests in tier 0:** R1058 (every detector on its fixture), R1059 (the FAIL detectors over the files the module
  serves, with the same baselines) and R1060 (the item tables' names and words with the module's live tables).
- **The review of texts written before the guide, `docs/dev/text-review-E65.md`.** The texts of the notice history (A7),
  of E77 and E78 (A8), of passages (A10), of the Frisk (A11) and of E70's trial modes, group by group: 216 rows (E66 32, E71 184), 130 of 407
  keys with a finding, from the lint's report and a reviewer agent. Nothing in `lang/` changes there; each row is fixed by
  the stage it names.
- **The pilot, `docs/dev/text-pilot.json`.** 40 texts chosen by the plan's quotas (tiles and config descriptions, toasts
  and player cards, settings hints, GM diagnostics, the world's voice, plural families), each written from its facts in
  English (172 facts; 3 more, checked in the code, were added after the writing: 175 in all), and in Polish from the
  facts without the new English, then reviewed in English, cold in English (without the old text) and in Polish, and
  revised once. The owner approved all 40. Of them, E66 applies 1 (a name) and
  E71 the other 39; the 60 naturalness pairs go to E66 where a pair changes a name and to E71 otherwise, and the lint
  reports each pair's old text until then.

## The repository's agent rules

The release commit adds to the repository's agent rules file at its root, as the owner answered Q-E65-1 ("Tak dopiszmy",
01.11.2026):

- **Before writing any user-facing text, read `docs/text-style.md` and `docs/glossary.json`.**
- **The Definition of Done rule:** a stage writes its new and changed texts to the guide and moves the English literals of
  the UI-rendering files it rewrites into i18n, in English and Polish; `diagnostics.mjs`'s console stays English; from
  E65 on, so not E29, E33 or E09-E19, whose files E71 sweeps (DB12).
- **`text` among the parts** of the "One check" row.

## Known gaps

- **The approved texts are not in the game.** The 40 and the 60 are in the guide and the pilot's file; `lang/` is as in
  1.2.94 until E66 (row 1.2.96) and E71 (row 1.2.128) apply them.
- **The Frisk row** still reads "Zobacz, co nosi" in Polish until E71 (above).
- **Rebuilt rules not yet confirmed:** 37 rules, section 3's other seven rows and section 12's method, to confirm in E71.
  The questions the pilot's reviewers left on O8, X6, X11, EN3, EN6, O5, M5, X4 and B2 stand on their defaults and go with
  E71's batch; X3, O9 and X7 stay unconfirmed because an approved text has their shape or a reviewer's point still waits.
- **The report detectors are not red.** At 52d91f38 they report 3414 findings; they turn to FAIL in E25, E66 and E71 as listed
  above. T4 and T19 place about a quarter of what they read ("T4 classified 2712 of 10242 (26.5%)", "T19 classified 1303
  of 4953 (26.3%)"), and nothing holds that share up; E71 decides whether T4's FAIL needs a floor.
- **The maps leave keys out:** 195 keys no screen reaches and 4070 no send reaches; E71 assigns what it needs.
- **The glossary's open entries:** `db3-english` and `mechanic-capitals` are settled by E25, `truth-bullet` and
  `murder-weapon` by E66, `gm-bar-buttons` by E71. Not in the glossary for want of a source: DB4's resources (E71) and
  "Find Stash" as a Polish form (E25).
- **Handed on, each to a stage with a ledger row:** the Polish strings that agree Eclipse and Overflow as masculine (E71);
  whether T20's FAIL also covers the other `Intl` formats (E66); T4 on the window surfaces by reader and T13's file set
  (E71); whether a Polish handbook that splits differently from the English one is red (E57, row 1.2.131).
- **Left as built from the end review:** a T6 baseline row of a script matches a bare sign anywhere in its file; T2 turns
  red on a correct Polish `.one` that names `{n}` where the English does not (the plan's rule); the pilot's quotas are not
  recorded in its file; the header of `scripts/tests.mjs` does not yet name `tests-text.mjs` (E66).
- **The handbook-facts trial** compared counts, not facts sentence by sentence, and the Polish handbook was not run. The
  reviewer agent's rows in the review of older texts are one agent's reading, which nothing re-checks.
- **Not measured:** CI, `npm test` as a whole, the local gate, the scenarios, the suite's skips against
  `skip-baseline.json`, and R1058 to R1060 in Foundry.

## Not checked at a real table yet

AUDIT section 9.2, item 361.

- **361, LIVE-E65-01:** on v14, as a GM whose module language is set to Polish (and the page reloaded),
  `game.drpg.runTests()` (tiers 0-1, writes nothing): R1060 and R972 both green, R1060's log line ending "0 config field(s)
  set and put back". The harness's GM plays in English, so there R1060 puts the Polish over the English itself and puts it
  back; that it reads the same on a Polish client follows from the code, not from a measurement.
